newsitem.title: UGANDA: Asian, Latin American coffees hurt Uganda's trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian, Latin American coffees hurt Uganda's trade.

text.p: Uganda's coffee traders are losing cash as the flow of Latin American and Asian supplies onto the world market has undermined prices in recent months.
Uganda's coffee also suffered because it lacked a brand name, traders said.
Frederick Kawuma, executive director of the Uganda Coffee Trade Federation (UCTF), said some traders had gone out of business.
"I talked to one UCTF member who invested 200 million shillings ($187,969) in coffee and he complained that he had registered losses up to 120 million shillings."

Kawuma said a flood of coffee from Latin America and Asia was behind the steady decline in prices. The past few weeks had been particularly difficult as most key producing countries were in harvest and there was no aggressive buying to lift prices.
Kawuma said Uganda urgently required a brand name.

"The biggest problem for Uganda is that it's Caffea Robusta, which accounts for 85-90 percent of Uganda's production and is ranked one of the best in the world, is not sold under a Ugandan label, hence it goes to the commodity exchange suffering serious price fluctuations," he said.
"The prices for coffee sold on the gourmet market are fairly constant and predictable. The basic problem is that Ugandans are seriously losing money -- mainly local traders," he said.
Uganda's coffee is produced mainly by around one million smallholders who cultivate some 274,000 hectares.
Although there were 117 registered coffee exporters in 1994/95, only about 50 were now active.

UCTF president Paul Mugambwa said, "We also see that specialty coffee is usually sold under labels and trade marks which very much help in giving identity in the market place to certain highly favoured origins and special blends."
He added, "Where a breakthrough has been made in this area, producers of such coffee always stand to gain from the proceeds from the sale of coffee that is sold to this sector of the market.
"We want the final user to identify our coffee. UCTF is vigorously trying to market the Ugandan robusta using the Internet, where they have opened a home page."
In June traders wrote to President Yoweri Museveni seeking his support in marketing Uganda's coffee under a brand name. Museveni has offered them no reply to date.
